method_notes: Breadth-first census built entirely from pages fetched live on 2026-09-20 via WebFetch/WebSearch: three Wikipedia capacity-list pages (rugby union stadiums, rugby league stadiums, cricket grounds by capacity) for population discovery, then per-venue Wikipedia infobox fetches for capacity, address, owner/operator and coordinates, then official venue sites for first-party calendar/event URLs. No capacity, URL, coordinate or venue name in this file was written from model memory: every figure traces to an 'evidence' entry naming a URL that was actually fetched. Authority grading is honest — GRADE_A means the venue's own site stated it, GRADE_B a per-venue Wikipedia infobox, GRADE_C an aggregate list page or a search-result summary. Known limitations: (1) coordinates and first-party calendar URLs are missing for most Championship-level rugby league grounds and several smaller county cricket grounds, because the time-box was spent on breadth rather than depth; (2) the Wikipedia rugby union list page is visibly stale (it still shows pre-rename stadium names and pre-2023 Premiership membership), so venues sourced only from it carry LOW confidence; (3) Stormont (Northern Ireland cricket) is included with a null capacity pending direct verification; (4) concert/conference calendar sources were only captured where a fetched official page actually exposed them.
